title: All-Time Great Indian Political Films
description: 25 landmark Indian films exploring elections, ideology, governance, corruption, political movements and the struggle for power.

entries.why_it_ranks: Mani Ratnam turns the relationship between cinema and Tamil Nadu politics into an extraordinary story of friendship, ideology, ambition and power, led by Mohanlal and Prakash Raj.
Gulzar combines political ambition with the collapse of a marriage, creating a remarkably human portrait of the personal cost of public life.
Jabbar Patel's uncompromising examination of politicians, journalists, bureaucracy and struggles for power remains one of Indian cinema's great political dramas.
One of India's sharpest political satires, exposing ideological fanaticism and party loyalty through the absurd conflict between two brothers.
A fearless satire of political power whose history became inseparable from the Emergency after the original prints were seized and destroyed.
Shankar converts the fantasy of an ordinary journalist becoming chief minister for a day into hugely entertaining political cinema with genuine questions about governance.
Politics, revolution, privilege and personal relationships collide against the turbulence of 1970s India.
Sekhar Kammula asks whether an idealistic individual can enter electoral politics without becoming part of the corruption he wants to eliminate.
A wonderfully understated examination of what democracy actually means when conducting an election becomes an exercise in bureaucracy, security and conflicting realities.
Mani Ratnam connects youth, violence, student activism and electoral politics through three intersecting lives.
Prakash Jha combines electoral politics, dynastic power and Mahabharata-style family warfare into one of modern Hindi cinema's strongest mainstream political dramas.
Political succession becomes a devastating family tragedy in which ambition and power gradually destroy almost every personal relationship.
The Hindi adaptation of Mudhalvan remains one of Bollywood's most memorable political entertainers, powered by Anil Kapoor and Amrish Puri.
Mani Ratnam's Hindi counterpart to Aayutha Ezhuthu explores how young Indians can move from political indifference toward participation.
A single deciding vote becomes a wonderfully funny and cutting examination of elections, caste and political opportunism.
Adoor Gopalakrishnan's complex examination of communist mythology, political memory and disillusionment is among India's most intellectually demanding political films.
Primarily remembered as a black comedy, but its satire of corruption, politicians, business and media makes it one of India's most enduring attacks on institutional power.
Youthful apathy transforms into political awakening as contemporary frustration becomes intertwined with memories of India's revolutionary movement.
Pa. Ranjith uses a neighbourhood wall to show how party politics, caste, identity and violence penetrate everyday community life.
Dibakar Banerjee examines development politics, corruption and the machinery protecting powerful interests through a tightly controlled political thriller.
Ram Gopal Varma combines family, extra-constitutional power and political influence into a dark drama dominated by Amitabh Bachchan.
Pa. Ranjith uses Rajinikanth's star persona to examine land, class, caste, political authority and resistance.
A provocative examination of media narratives, manufactured public anger and the political exploitation of popular sentiment.
An unusually serious mainstream Telugu examination of bureaucracy, electoral power and the limitations faced by an honest civil servant.
Journalism, elections and political manipulation come together in an exceptionally entertaining political thriller.
